sentences.en: It says, there's a comment, slash slash, we must prepare for his coming, everything's lowercase except for the H in his, and then struct Gozer,
sentences.zh: 上面写着，有个注释，双斜杠，我们必须为他的降临做好准备，除了"his"中的"H"以外全是小写，然后是结构体Gozer，

sentences.en: and it's a function object that calls something's destructor.
sentences.zh: 它是一个调用某个对象析构函数的函数对象。

sentences.en: Well, the comment made more sense because I think that used to be a forward declaration.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个注释更有意义，因为我觉得那以前是个前向声明。

sentences.en: So, obviously, this is a Ghostbusters reference.
sentences.zh: 所以，很明显，这是一个《捉鬼敢死队》的彩蛋。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 242, recorded on May 21st, 2025.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收看 ADSP 播客第 242 期，录制于 2025 年 5 月 21 日。

sentences.en: My name is Conor, and today with my co-host, Bryce, we finish part four of our four-part conversation with Jared Hoverock.
sentences.zh: 我是康纳，今天与我的联合主持人布莱斯一起，我们完成了与贾里德·霍弗洛克的四部分对话的第四部分。

sentences.en: We chat about thrust, parallel algorithms, and more.
sentences.zh: 我们聊了 Thrust、并行算法等等。

sentences.en: That actually kind of leads to another question that I had meant to ask earlier, which is,
sentences.zh: 这其实引出了我之前一直想问的另一个问题，那就是，

sentences.en: you talked a little bit about the transfer of thrust from research to production in the handoff.
sentences.zh: 你之前稍微谈到了在交接过程中将 Thrust 从研究转化为生产的过程。

sentences.en: But that was sort of after thrust had, you know, sort of made it, you know.
sentences.zh: 但那差不多是在 Thrust 已经，你知道的，差不多成功之后了。

sentences.en: And, you know, at the time, there were a couple other libraries that were kind of similar to thrust, like CUDPP.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当时还有好几个类似于 Thrust 的库，比如 CUDPP。

sentences.en: And I think there was like one or two other ones.
sentences.zh: 我想还有另外一两个吧。

sentences.en: And I just wonder, like, can you tell us a little bit about when you guys first put thrust out there?
sentences.zh: 我就想知道，能不能跟我们聊聊你们最初推出 Thrust 的时候？

sentences.en: Like, what was the response?
sentences.zh: 比如，反响怎么样？

sentences.en: Was it like, did it just very rapidly get a lot of adoption and grow in popularity?
sentences.zh: 是不是很快就得到了广泛采用并越来越受欢迎？

sentences.en: And like, what, why was it that thrust is the one that succeeded and became so ubiquitous?
sentences.zh: 还有就是，为什么最后成功并变得如此无处不在的是 Thrust？

sentences.en: And like, how quickly did that happen?
sentences.zh: 这个过程有多快？

sentences.en: I mean, the reason it succeeded is because we chose the right interface.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它成功的原因是我们选择了正确的接口。

sentences.en: How fast it happened, I don't really remember.
sentences.zh: 至于多快发生的，我记不太清了。

sentences.en: I remember we gave, at the first GTC, we gave like two talks on thruSt.
sentences.zh: 我记得在第一届 GTC 上，我们关于 Thrust 做了一两次演讲。

sentences.en: And I remember the crowd being large and enthusiastic.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时人山人海，非常热情。

sentences.en: So it at least had succeeded enough to attract some, you know, some people to a talk.
sentences.zh: 所以它至少已经成功到足以吸引一些人来听讲座了。

sentences.en: Do you have the slides from those talks?
sentences.zh: 你有那些演讲的幻灯片吗？

sentences.en: Somewhere.
sentences.zh: 在某处吧。

sentences.en: They might be.
sentences.zh: 可能在吧。

sentences.en: Are they not in the repository?
sentences.zh: 难道不在代码仓库里吗？

sentences.en: They might not be.
sentences.zh: 可能不在。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Oh, I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 哦，我觉得没有。

sentences.en: They're probably in Perforce somewhere.
sentences.zh: 它们可能在 Perforce 的某个地方。

sentences.en: If you look through Perforce, you'll find them.
sentences.zh: 如果你翻翻 Perforce，就能找到它们。

sentences.en: Or I might have them in like a Google Drive or something like that.
sentences.zh: 或者我可能把它们放在谷歌云端硬盘之类的地方。

sentences.en: Anyway, yeah, they were, Nathan gave a talk and I gave a talk at the GTC.
sentences.zh: 总之，对，它们，内森在 GTC 上做了一个演讲，我也做了一个。

sentences.en: And Nathan's talk was sort of, here's what thrust is.
sentences.zh: 内森的演讲大概是，这就是 Thrust。

sentences.en: And I think my talk was like, here's how to do some, you know, interesting tricks with thruSt.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我的演讲大概是，这里有一些关于 Thrust 的有趣小技巧。

sentences.en: And it's just, you know, walk, the slides just walk through some of the example prograMs.
sentences.zh: 然后就是，你知道的，浏览一下，幻灯片只是过了一遍一些示例程序。

sentences.en: But, so how long, so like after that, did you ever reach a point where you guys were just like swamped with PRs and like, when did you,
sentences.zh: 那么，用了多久，也就是说在那之后，你们有没有遇到过被各种 PR 淹没的时候，然后你们是何时，

sentences.en: when did it become like visible to you that there were a lot of people using this?
sentences.zh: 你们是什么时候发现有这么多人正在使用它的？

sentences.en: And when did, like, when did the writing, was the writing on the wall that like it was going to have to be taken over by the engineering team?
sentences.zh: 而且，迹象是什么时候出现的，也就是注定必须由工程团队接管的迹象？

sentences.en: It never became visible to me that a lot of people were using it.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有觉得有很多人在用它。

sentences.en: I would have been happy to, I, Nathan was really pro productization because, you know, for career reasons, I would have rather not productize it so we could continue, you know,
sentences.zh: 我本来挺乐意的，我，内森真的很支持产品化，因为出于职业原因，我其实宁愿不把它产品化，这样我们就可以继续，你知道的，

sentences.en: developing it in interesting directions.
sentences.zh: 朝着有趣的方向开发它。

sentences.en: I guess, I guess the problem is when it got productized, it's became less flexible, like changing it became harder, harder, you know, before we actually released it on Google code,
sentences.zh: 我想，我想问题在于当它产品化之后，它变得不那么灵活了，比如修改它变得越来越难，你知道的，在我们真正在谷歌代码上发布它之前，

sentences.en: like GitHub didn't even exist at the time.
sentences.zh: 就像当时甚至还没有 GitHub。

sentences.en: So the initial release was on Google code.
sentences.zh: 所以最初的版本是在 Google Code 上发布的。

sentences.en: And if we wanted to change something, we would just change something.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想改点什么，我们就会直接改。

sentences.en: And if people had a bug, we would fix it as, you know, next day or something like that.
sentences.zh: 如果人们遇到了 Bug，我们就会在第二天左右修复它。

sentences.en: You can't really do that with a product.
sentences.zh: 做产品可不能这样。

sentences.en: But, I don't know, like hearing you guys talk about it, or hearing you guys talk about people out in the wild using it, I guess, is when it dawned on me that it has a lot of users.
sentences.zh: 但是，我不知道，听到你们谈论它，或者听到你们谈论外界的人在使用它，我想我才恍然大悟，原来它有这么多的用户。

sentences.en: Like at the time, it just seemed like, you know, a project we were working on, and we're happy to work on.
sentences.zh: 就像当时，它看起来只像是我们正在进行的、且乐于从事的一个项目。

sentences.en: Yeah, I was, I was, I sort of always had that sense.
sentences.zh: 对，我，我一直都有这种感觉。

sentences.en: And I mean, I guess it's, it's hard for folks who sit and research, because you, you produce a thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想对于坐在实验室里做研究的人来说挺难的，因为你创造了一个东西。

sentences.en: And then if it becomes marginally successful, then it gets picked up by, you know, some engineering team.
sentences.zh: 然后如果它取得了一点成功，它就会被，你知道的，某个工程团队接手。

sentences.en: And you, then you go work on the next thing, and you don't necessarily see what the...
sentences.zh: 然后你，然后你就去研究下一个东西了，你并不一定能看到...

sentences.en: I think it works differently now.
sentences.zh: 我觉得现在情况不太一样了。

sentences.en: So Thrust was one of the first things that Envy Research productized.
sentences.zh: 所以 Thrust 是英伟达研究院首批产品化的项目之一。

sentences.en: And we didn't have a lot of experience with handing off things to product teaMs.
sentences.zh: 我们当时对如何将东西移交给产品团队并没有太多经验。

sentences.en: So I think if it were to happen today, researchers could be involved in the product, like to the extent that they're interested in.
sentences.zh: 所以我想如果今天发生这种情况，研究人员可以参与到产品中，程度取决于他们的兴趣。

sentences.en: But in those days, it was sort of seen as like, okay, you guys productize this thing.
sentences.zh: 但在那个年代，这基本上被视为，好吧，你们这东西产品化了。

sentences.en: It's time to work on something, something new.
sentences.zh: 该去研究新东西了。

sentences.en: So, but I think, since then, people probably see the value of keeping the original authors sort of in the loop, maybe a bit more, if they want to be, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，不过我认为，从那以后，人们可能看到了让原作者在某种程度上更多地参与进来的价值，如果他们愿意的话，你知道的，

sentences.en: with more recent projects.
sentences.zh: 对于更新的项目来说是这样的。

sentences.en: Are you proud of Thrust?
sentences.zh: 你为 Thrust 感到骄傲吗？

sentences.en: I have mixed feelings about it.
sentences.zh: 我对它百感交集。

sentences.en: Like, I guess what I see is the sort of missed opportunities.
sentences.zh: 比如，我看到的是各种错失的良机。

sentences.en: And I sort of see the mistakes that could be corrected or should have been corrected.
sentences.zh: 我看到了那些本可以纠正或应该纠正的错误。

sentences.en: But it's, I mean, it's gratifying to see that people still like to use it and think it's worthwhile.
sentences.zh: 但是，看到人们仍然喜欢使用它并认为它有价值，这还是挺令人欣慰的。

sentences.en: But it's hard not to focus on things you wish could have been done better.
sentences.zh: 但很难不把注意力放在那些你希望可以做得更好的事情上。

sentences.en: One frequent thing that gets brought up is, well, Thrust is great for many things, and it's a great place to start.
sentences.zh: 一个经常被提及的问题是，嗯，Thrust 在很多方面都很棒，而且是一个很好的起点。

sentences.en: If you're doing, if your algorithm ends up being one, you know, call, it's a single pass thing.
sentences.zh: 如果你在做，如果你的算法最终只需要一次，你知道的，调用，它是一个单遍的过程。

sentences.en: Thrust is perfect for that.
sentences.zh: Thrust 对此简直完美。

sentences.en: If you're launching multiple things because Thrust doesn't have an asynchrony model, because it blocks, it can become a performance bottleneck.
sentences.zh: 如果你启动了多个东西，因为 Thrust 没有异步模型，因为它会阻塞，这就会成为一个性能瓶颈。

sentences.en: That's something that is an often cited criticism of ThruSt.
sentences.zh: 这是对 Thrust 经常被引用的批评。

sentences.en: And we sometimes think of it as being an on-ramp for parallelism that it's something that's easy and gets people started.
sentences.zh: 我们有时认为它是通往并行性的一条便捷通道，它很简单，能让人们上手。

sentences.en: But oftentimes, if you need to architect a much more complex application where you're launching a bunch of different kernels,
sentences.zh: 但通常情况下，如果你需要架构一个更复杂的应用程序，需要启动一堆不同的核函数，

sentences.en: then you have to go and do something a little bit lower level.
sentences.zh: 那么你就必须去做一些更底层的事情。

sentences.en: And had Thrust evolved earlier and more to support asynchrony in a more structured way, perhaps it could have been even more successful than it is today.
sentences.zh: 如果 Thrust 能更早、更全面地以一种更有结构的方式支持异步，也许它会比今天取得更大的成功。

sentences.en: Oh, for sure.
sentences.zh: 哦，那肯定。

sentences.en: And Thrust predates asynchrony in CUDA.
sentences.zh: 而且 Thrust 出现的时间比 CUDA 中的异步功能还要早。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Thrust predates CUDA streams, right?
sentences.zh: Thrust 比 CUDA 流出现得更早，对吧？

sentences.en: So, and it was always not clear how to make it work well with CUDA streams, and I don't think it ever really did or does work well with CUDA streaMs.
sentences.zh: 所以，而且一直不清楚如何让它与 CUDA 流很好地配合，我不认为它过去或现在真的能与 CUDA 流很好地配合。

sentences.en: I guess another regret is that in addition to Thrust, we also have CUDA, and these two things have interdependencies, like they're cyclic dependencies between the two libraries,
sentences.zh: 我想另一个遗憾是，除了 Thrust，我们还有 CUDA，这两者之间存在相互依赖，比如这两个库之间存在循环依赖，

sentences.en: which causes probleMs.
sentences.zh: 这会导致问题。

sentences.en: I guess it's just a shame that we couldn't find a way to do CUDA-like things in Thrust, or, you know, Thrust-like things in CUDA.
sentences.zh: 我想遗憾的是我们没能在 Thrust 中找到实现类似 CUDA 功能的方法，或者说，在 CUDA 中实现类似 Thrust 功能的方法。

sentences.en: So, it's sort of an awkward situation to have most libraries.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于大多数库来说，这算是一个尴尬的处境。

sentences.en: Well, and it's actually interesting that you mentioned that because, you know, we, so when I started at NVIDIA in 2017, I was,
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实你提到这个很有趣，因为，你知道，我们，当我 2017 年加入英伟达时，我，

sentences.en: Thrust had been essentially without a maintainer for like two or three years.
sentences.zh: Thrust 基本上已经有两三年没有维护者了。

sentences.en: And like on day one, I didn't even know what I was being hired to do when I started.
sentences.zh: 刚入职的第一天，我甚至不知道自己被招来做什么。

sentences.en: Like, it was unclear from the job description, but, and like, my hiring was weird, but just like Olivier had talked to someone and been like, hey, you should interview this guy.
sentences.zh: 职位描述里写得不是很清楚，而且我被招聘的过程也很诡异，就是奥利维耶跟某人谈过，然后说，嘿，你应该面试这家伙。

sentences.en: And then I interviewed, and then they're like, oh, you want a job?
sentences.zh: 然后我面试了，接着他们说，哦，你想要份工作吗？

sentences.en: And they gave me an offer, and then I showed up, and on day one, they're like, so here's this thing, Thrust, you're now in charge of it.
sentences.zh: 他们向我发出了录用通知，然后我去了公司，在第一天，他们说，好了，这是 Thrust，你现在负责它。

sentences.en: There's no product manager.
sentences.zh: 没有产品经理。

sentences.en: Nobody's really touched it in two years.
sentences.zh: 两年里根本没人碰过它。

sentences.en: Figure out what to do with it.
sentences.zh: 自己想想要怎么处理它。

sentences.en: And so, then I started the CUDA C++ Core Libraries team at NVIDIA, and originally it was just me, and then it was me and one other person for some period of time.
sentences.zh: 于是，我在英伟达创立了 CUDA C++ 核心库团队，最初只有我一个人，后来在一段时间里是我和另外一个人。

sentences.en: And we productized Cub just as Thrust had been productized and did some amount of work to unify things between the two.
sentences.zh: 我们把 Cub 产品化了，就像当年 Thrust 被产品化一样，并且做了一些工作来统一两者的东西。

sentences.en: But now, you know, eight years later, that team, the CUDA C++ Core Libraries team, or I think it's now just the Core Compute Libraries team, same acronym, but different meaning.
sentences.zh: 但现在，你知道，八年过去了，那个团队，CUDA C++ 核心库团队，或者我想现在它只是核心计算库团队，缩写一样，但含义不同。

sentences.en: It's now like a, I don't know, it's more than 10 people team.
sentences.zh: 它现在是一个，我不知道，超过 10 人的团队。

sentences.en: It could be 15 people or so.
sentences.zh: 大概有 15 人左右吧。

sentences.en: So, it's a lot of people working on it, and they work on Thrust, Cub, and LibC++, which is our port of LibC++.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多人在上面工作，他们负责 Thrust、Cub 和 LibC++，后者是我们对 LibC++ 的移植版本。

sentences.en: And there's a move for all three of these libraries to essentially merge together into one unified thing.
sentences.zh: 并且这三个库正朝着本质上合并为一个统一实体的方向发展。

sentences.en: And they're all living now, a monorepo now, and in fact, there's some talk about the, not the Thrust name.
sentences.zh: 它们现在都存放在一个单体代码仓库中，事实上，有人讨论过，不是 Thrust 这个名字。

sentences.en: The Thrust name will essentially always exist because there's so many people who have written code for it.
sentences.zh: Thrust 这个名字基本上会永远存在，因为有太多人为它编写过代码。

sentences.en: But of migrating the Thrust backend and sort of merging it with some of the other things.
sentences.zh: 而是要迁移 Thrust 后端并将其与一些其他东西合并。

sentences.en: So, the Thrust code base, parts of the Thrust code base that have been around for a long time now, essentially going away in the future.
sentences.zh: 所以，Thrust 代码库中存在了很长时间的一部分代码，在未来基本上会消失。

sentences.en: And all of these things merging together into a more unified structure down the road.
sentences.zh: 所有这些东西将来都会合并到一个更统一的结构中。

sentences.en: I think the last thing I'd ask you about is Thrust was open source sort of from the start.
sentences.zh: 我想我要问你的最后一件事情是，Thrust 几乎从一开始就是开源的。

sentences.en: And, you know, like, what was that like?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，那是一种怎样的体验？

sentences.en: I mean, this was in a very, you know, an early time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是在一个非常，你知道，非常早期的时代。

sentences.en: It was before, you know, before GitHub.
sentences.zh: 那是在，你知道的，在 GitHub 出现之前。

sentences.en: You mentioned it was, like, Google Code.
sentences.zh: 你提到过，就像 Google Code 一样。

sentences.en: But, like, how did you collaborate with people back in the day?
sentences.zh: 但是，当年你们是怎么跟别人合作的？

sentences.en: Like, how did users find you?
sentences.zh: 比如，用户是怎么找到你们的？

sentences.en: How did you interact?
sentences.zh: 你们是怎么互动的？

sentences.en: Like, what was that like?
sentences.zh: 那是一种什么样的体验？

sentences.en: We had a Google Groups mailing list that people would ask, how do I do this in Thrust, that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个 Google 集团邮件列表，人们会在上面问，我怎么在 Thrust 里实现这个，诸如此类的问题。

sentences.en: Or maybe they would report bugs.
sentences.zh: 或者他们会报告 Bug。

sentences.en: There wasn't, like, use Discord or Slack or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 当时没有什么 Discord 或 Slack 之类的东西。

sentences.en: So just through, you know, mailing lists, I guess that's how people used to collaborate in the 2000s, you know, through a mailing list or something like that.
sentences.zh: 所以只能通过，你知道的，邮件列表，我想这就是 2000 年代人们合作的方式，通过邮件列表之类的东西。

sentences.en: I remember when we pushed the code for the first time, we announced it on Hacker News and some subreddit and just, you know, waiting to see what would happen.
sentences.zh: 我记得我们第一次推送代码时，我们在 Hacker News 和某个 subreddit 上进行了官宣，然后，你知道的，就等着看会发生什么。

sentences.en: But as far as I know, Thrust was the first open source thing that NVIDIA ever published.
sentences.zh: 但据我所知，Thrust 是英伟达发布的第一个开源项目。

sentences.en: I don't know of any that are – there might be a few previous publications, but I don't know of them.
sentences.zh: 我不知道有没有——可能之前有过几次发布，但我不知道。

sentences.en: So that was – you know, we had to get special permission for that.
sentences.zh: 所以那是——你知道的，我们必须为此获得特别许可。

sentences.en: You are, in fact, correct that Thrust was, in fact, the first open source project at NVIDIA.
sentences.zh: 事实上你说得对，Thrust 确实是英伟达的第一个开源项目。

sentences.en: And we know this because Thrust completely predated any open source process at NVIDIA.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以知道这一点，是因为 Thrust 完全早于英伟达的任何开源流程。

sentences.en: And every, like, year or two, somebody's like, hey, like, why isn't there, like, an entry in, like, our listing of open source things, like, in this database for Thrust?
sentences.zh: 然后每隔一两年，就会有人问，嘿，为什么在我们的开源项目清单里，比如这个数据库里，没有 Thrust 的条目？

sentences.en: And we're like, well, because it was the first one.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就说，嗯，因为它这是第一个。

sentences.en: Like, it existed before all these things.

sentences.zh: 杰瑞德，这些是——我一直很好奇这个，所以我索性问了，尽管我们时间有点超，但为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Two things I'll ask.
sentences.zh: 我有两件事要问。

sentences.en: One, it thrusts a lot of these headers that are .inl, like inline.
sentences.zh: 第一，Thrust 的许多头文件都是 .inl 后缀，类似于内联。

sentences.zh: 这是因为你曾经有些人会——把这些包含在他们的 .cpp 文件里，而你想把它们从声明中分离出来吗？

sentences.en: Or was there at some point a built,
sentences.zh: 或者曾经有过一个构建版本，

sentences.en: like a version of Thrust that had like a mode where you – just like boost ASIO where you could build like a library version of it in addition to the header-only version?
sentences.zh: 比如某种模式的 Thrust 版本——就像 Boost.Asio 那样，除了只包含头文件的版本外，你还可以构建它的库版本？

sentences.zh: 或者像这种 .inl 命名的惯例究竟意味着什么？

sentences.zh: 我觉得那只是杰瑞德主义（Jaredism）。

sentences.zh: 我不记得我为什么选择这样做。

sentences.zh: 但至少在某个时候，有一个目标，就是你可以用普通的 C++ 编译器包含任何 Thrust 头文件，而它不会崩溃。

sentences.en: And I don't know if that's still the case, but there wasn't – you didn't have to include it with MVCC, so it seemed unnecessary to –
sentences.zh: 我不知道现在还是不是这样，但当时——你不必用 NVCC 包含它，所以似乎没必要——

sentences.en: That's actually – it's a good point that we didn't talk about this, but Thrust has this back-end system that we mentioned,
sentences.zh: 这其实——说得很有道理，我们之前没聊过这个，但 Thrust 有我们提到过的这种后端系统，

sentences.zh: 但我们没有明确讨论的一个事实是，Thrust 可以针对 CPU。

sentences.zh: 因为在调试程序的正确性时，能够使用顺序后端或者比如 OpenMP 后端，这真的很有帮助。

sentences.zh: 我通常会用 printf，因为当我在调试某些东西时，通常来说，如果它不是一个并行 Bug，
